correctness.rationale: All candidate parent sources correspond exactly to 2k-palindromic windows and their deletions. The seam equality formula is exact; two reflected length-2k windows at separation s give period 2s, forcing identical parents for s=1 and for 2s|k. Thus representative starts are separated by s_k and give the bound. A binary 2s_k-periodic witness supports all spaced starts, and the first-d-step mismatch on either parity class proves pairwise distinct outcomes; all indices and edge cases q>=2, k>=1, m>=2k have been checked. The packaged finite program corroborates the infinite proof but is not the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2017 primary results bound arbitrary-length palindromic deletion spheres by runs of valid positions, with exact small-length cases; they do not establish the new sharp arithmetic all-k worst-case inverse-degree formula or the matching periodic witness. The present result is a strict nontrivial extremal optimization beyond those bounds. Named related channels and broader code-capacity results do not imply the claimed list extremum. Residual risk of an unidentified equivalence persists.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent specialization of palindrome-test matrix bounds or other classical overlap combinatorics could exist without the searched terminology.
The complete text of later arXiv:2609.00779 could not be inspected; the accessible abstract studies two-error forward descendants and makes a direct match unlikely.
The first-public-source date belongs to the 2017 guiding primary paper, not a publication claim about the present result.

value.rationale: The all-length exact worst-case inverse list is a natural synchronization-decoding invariant, not an arbitrary slice. The optimal spacing depends nontrivially on divisibility of duplication length; period-2s_k binary constructions attain sharpness across all alphabets and lengths. The result resolves this complete extremal question, while not claiming code-rate improvements or multi-error consequences.
